line: U.S. stocks hit fresh record highs as tech led a broad rally.
details: The S&P 500 rose about 1.8% to a new all-time high near 7,737, the Dow gained about 1.7% to roughly 54,086, and the Nasdaq jumped about 2.6%. Strong earnings and cooler oil prices helped push risk appetite higher across Wall Street.

line: Oil plunged as markets bet on a Strait of Hormuz reopening.
details: Brent crude fell about 6% toward the high-$70s after U.S. officials said a deal to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could come soon. Lower oil eases inflation worries and can help airlines, while energy producers often face pressure.

line: Chip stocks surged, with semiconductors up more than 7% in a day.
details: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped over 7% as AI optimism returned. ARM climbed roughly 17%, while Intel and other chip names gained more than 10% in the session as investors piled back into the group.

line: Palantir soared about 29% after a blowout earnings report.
details: Palantir said revenue jumped about 93% and U.S. commercial growth ran even hotter. Traders rewarded the beat with a huge one-day jump, though the stock still trades at a very rich valuation after the move.

line: AMD beat earnings, then slipped after hours on guidance.
details: AMD posted record quarterly revenue near $11.5 billion and strong data-center growth, but shares fell more than 8% after hours. Investors wanted an even hotter third-quarter outlook than the company guided.

line: Treasury yields fell as cooler oil eased rate-hike fears.
details: Lower crude prices helped pull bond yields down, with the 10-year yield dropping several basis points. Banks and other rate-sensitive stocks can move when traders change their Fed outlook.

line: Anthropic locked in a $10 billion AI computing deal.
details: Claude maker Anthropic signed a multi-year computing-power agreement worth about $10 billion with a cloud infrastructure partner. Big AI compute contracts keep demand high for chips, cloud, and data-center suppliers.

line: Chipotle beat sales, then got hit by a salmonella scare.
details: Chipotle raised guidance after a solid quarter and the stock jumped, but headlines about a Minnesota salmonella outbreak later pulled shares back. Food-safety news can quickly outweigh an earnings beat.

line: Energy stocks faced pressure as crude tumbled.
details: With WTI settling around $75 and Brent near $79 after sharp drops, oil producers and oilfield-service names often lag when traders expect cheaper crude. The flip side is relief for consumers and many non-energy stocks.

line: Mega-cap tech helped lift markets after a rough July.
details: Technology shares jumped around 4% in the record session as investors returned to AI leaders. Mega-cap names still drive a large share of S&P 500 moves when the group rallies or sells off together.

line: Software and cloud names rode the AI spending wave higher.
details: Enterprise software and cloud platforms benefited as markets bought into continued AI investment. Strong backlog and compute demand remain key themes for the group even when individual names swing after earnings.

line: Industrials gained nearly 2% with the risk-on move.
details: Lower oil and stronger equity risk appetite helped industrials and materials advance. Broad market rallies often lift cyclical names that track growth and shipping demand.

line: Financials advanced as Goldman Sachs jumped more than 3%.
details: The financial sector rose about 1% in the record session, with Goldman Sachs among the stronger bank names. Trading desks and investment banks often benefit when markets are busy and volatility stays orderly.

line: Roku earnings day approaches under the Fox buyout deal.
details: Roku is set to report results around early August, but the pending Fox acquisition can keep the stock pinned near the deal price. Takeover situations often mute the usual earnings reaction until the sale closes.

line: Auto and EV names tracked the broader risk rally.
details: With the Nasdaq leading the day, growth-sensitive consumer and auto stocks often move with tech. Lower fuel costs can also help the consumer backdrop if cheaper oil sticks.

line: Media and streaming stocks rode the market higher.
details: Risk-on sessions usually lift consumer and media names along with the indexes. Investors still separate companies with improving profits from those facing slower subscriber growth.

line: Gig and delivery platforms watched consumer spending strength.
details: Cheaper oil and a stronger equity tape can support travel and dining activity that feeds delivery and ride volumes. These stocks still swing with growth expectations and deal headlines.

line: Retailers remain split between resilient spending and softer growth.
details: A broad market rally helps sentiment, but names with slowing comps or tough competition can still lag. Investors keep watching whether consumers keep spending as energy prices ease.

line: Payments stocks benefit when markets and travel activity improve.
details: Card networks earn more when consumer and cross-border spending stay firm. A risk-on tape and lower oil can support that backdrop, though the group still depends on the next round of spending data.
